name: attitude-gain
hypothesis: Both crashes show large body tilt at impact (0.39 rad and -0.29 rad with legs touching), i.e. the controller under-reacts to attitude error under crosswind turbulence. Amplifying the angle and angular-rate inputs (x1.6) should make the side-engine corrections kick in earlier and keep the lander upright through touchdown.

name: horizontal-gain
hypothesis: Increasing attitude gain backfired: the lander over-corrects tilt and drifts downwind (one crash at x=0.78 with no horizontal recovery). The dominant failure under crosswind is horizontal drift: crashes show |vx|~0.5 at impact and even safe landings end far off pad (x=0.44, -0.26). Amplifying the horizontal position and velocity inputs (x1.5) should make the controller fight the crosswind drift earlier and touch down closer to the pad.

name: rate-damping
hypothesis: Horizontal gain didn't fix the crashes: they still end with large angular velocity (-0.53, -0.29, -0.23 rad/s) and tilt at touchdown. The earlier angle+rate gain of 1.6 overcorrected the attitude itself; instead I'll only amplify the angular-rate input (x1.5), adding pure rotational damping so the lander doesn't tip over during the turbulent final descent while keeping the original attitude targeting.

name: rate-damping-strong
hypothesis: Rate damping x1.5 improved safe landings to 4/6 and the two remaining crashes both end with residual angular velocity ~-0.37 rad/s at leg contact (the lander touches down tilted and tips over), while every safe landing ends with rate ~0. The damping is still too weak; doubling the angular-rate input gain (x2.2) should suppress the tip-over at touchdown.

name: rate-damping-mild
hypothesis: Rate damping is non-monotonic: x1.5 gave 4/6 safe landings but x2.2 collapsed (1/6, with truncations from excessive side-engine chatter). The gain is too aggressive past ~1.5. A milder x1.25 damping may preserve the original's 2 solved episodes while still suppressing the tip-over crashes.

name: main-bias
hypothesis: Mild rate damping (x1.25) roughly matches the original (2 solved) but the persistent crash pattern is a late, low-altitude leftward drift (vx~-0.57 at h~0.19) that cannot be corrected before touchdown. Raising the main-engine logit bias (+0.3) should make the controller brake the descent harder and buy time for the side engines to arrest drift and level the body before contact.

name: rate-damp-plus-main-bias
hypothesis: Two single changes each gave 4/6 safe landings: angular-rate damping x1.25 (suppresses tip-over) and main-engine bias +0.3 (harder braking, more time for lateral correction). They act on different failure modes, so combining them should be complementary: stronger braking during the turbulent final descent while keeping rotation damped at touchdown.

name: combo-plus-vx-gain
hypothesis: Rate damping x1.25 + main bias +0.3 is the best so far (5/6 safe, mean 133). The single remaining crash shows an unrecovered late leftward drift (vx=-0.78, spin 1.15 at contact) starting around h~0.2. Adding a moderate horizontal-velocity input gain (x1.4) on top should make the side engines counter that drift earlier, without the full x-gain x1.5 that previously hurt.

name: combo-rate15
hypothesis: Adding the vx gain broke the combo (2/6 safe), so horizontal-velocity scaling is harmful in this regime. Returning to the winning combo but with slightly stronger rate damping (x1.5 instead of x1.25): the combo's one crash ended with spin 1.15 rad/s at contact, and x1.5 damping alone previously eliminated exactly that tip-over mode; the main-engine bias should counteract the over-rotation/chatter that x1.5 caused on its own.

name: combo-plus-angle
hypothesis: Rate x1.5 with the bias is clearly worse (2/6), so the x1.25 damping level is right. The winning combo still lands tilted on several safe episodes (0.37 rad at x=-0.33) and its one crash ends with spin 1.15. A small body-angle input gain (x1.15) on top of the combo should tighten attitude tracking toward upright at touchdown without the overcorrection that the x1.6 angle gain caused.

name: combo-bias045
hypothesis: The angle gain also hurt; the winning combo (rate x1.25 + main bias +0.3, 5/6 safe, mean 133) remains best. Its one crash is a late low-altitude drift/spin at contact, suggesting descent is still slightly too fast in the final phase. Increasing the main-engine bias to +0.45 should brake the last 0.2m of descent harder, giving the side engines more time to null drift and spin before touchdown.

name: combo-rate135
hypothesis: Bias 0.45 collapsed (2/6), confirming +0.3 is the right braking level. With bias fixed at 0.3, safe rate peaks between rate gains: 1.0 gives 4/6, 1.25 gives 5/6, 1.5 gives 2/6. Probing rate gain 1.35 with bias 0.3 to see if the optimum lies just above 1.25 for suppressing the residual touchdown spin.
